column1: 28 | PART I Introduction Newcomers to macroeconomics are sometimes confused by how macroeconomists use familiar words in new and specific ways. One example is the term “investment.” The confusion arises because what looks like investment for an individual may not be investment for the economy as a whole. The general rule is that the economy’s investment does not include purchases that merely reallocate existing assets among different individuals. Investment, as macroeconomists use the term, creates a new physical asset, called capital, which can be used in future production.
